title: CMB Thermodynamic Interpretation: A Compatibility and Null-Test Framework Under Entropy-Constrained Structure Formation
abstract: CMB compatibility framework for EFC with null tests: theta_s within 0.5%, damping scale within 5%, A_L in 0.9-0.95 range. Predictions for ISW phase shift and lensing evolution. JWST observations constrain S(z) which is tested against CMB constraints without parameter fitting.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper constructs a systematic null-test and compatibility framework for EFC's thermodynamic interpretation of the CMB, testing whether Planck data (TT/TE/EE power spectra, lensing, ISW) are consistent with entropy-constrained structure formation. It does not introduce new kill criteria or sealed predictions, but it provides an empirical scaffolding that quantifies how well the entropy-profile mechanism reproduces known CMB observables and identifies where EFC-specific deviations could appear. The framework also connects forward to JWST early-structure phenomenology by establishing the entropy baseline against which high-redshift anomalies would be measured.
graph_insights: Graph shows this paper touches CMB, Planck, lensing, ISW, entropy profile, and JWST but has no 1-hop or 2-hop connections to existing papers — it is a new node that bridges the CMB-observable cluster to the entropy/thermodynamic-interpretation cluster, creating a previously absent link in the knowledge graph.

The absence of connections to validation tests sharing observables confirms this is genuinely new infrastructure: no prior EFC paper performed dedicated CMB null tests at this level of systematization.

The JWST tag suggests the authors explicitly intend forward coupling to early-structure phenomenology, even though the paper is CMB-focused — this is a deliberate bridge node that should be linked to the phenomenology-jwst-early-structure gap in the graph.

language_hedges.raw_claim: EFC's thermodynamic interpretation is compatible with all Planck CMB observables
language_hedges.hedged_version: Within the null-test framework examined, EFC's entropy-constrained structure formation passes Planck TT/TE/EE, lensing, and ISW consistency checks at the precision currently tested; this establishes compatibility but does not constitute a unique proof of the thermodynamic mechanism.
language_hedges.reason: Compatibility / null-test pass ≠ proof of uniqueness; the result is within-class consistency, not a universality demonstration.

language_hedges.raw_claim: The entropy profile reproduces CMB spectra
language_hedges.hedged_version: The entropy-constrained profile is consistent with Planck CMB spectra to the precision of the current null-test suite; reproduction at the level distinguishable from ΛCDM awaits EFCLASS Boltzmann-solver implementation and Stage-IV data.
language_hedges.reason: Structural consistency claim should not be elevated to point-prediction validation without a full Boltzmann solver; the paper uses a null-test framework, not a fit with free parameters optimized.

language_hedges.raw_claim: ISW signal validates EFC's late-time entropy evolution
language_hedges.hedged_version: The observed ISW cross-correlation amplitude is consistent with EFC's predicted late-time entropy evolution within current error bars; definitive validation requires higher-S/N ISW measurements from upcoming surveys.
language_hedges.reason: ISW is notoriously noisy (~4σ detection); 'validates' overstates current statistical power — 'consistent with' is appropriate.

ledger_impact.narrative_frame_reason: The paper does not close a kill criterion or open a new one; it clarifies the empirical footing of EFC's thermodynamic CMB channel by building the null-test infrastructure needed before Stage-IV data arrive.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_sentence: A dedicated CMB null-test framework now quantifies EFC's thermodynamic compatibility with Planck TT/TE/EE, lensing, and ISW, establishing the entropy-profile baseline for upcoming Stage-IV and JWST confrontations.
implicit_consequences: The entropy-profile baseline established here becomes the mandatory starting point for the JWST early-structure prediction paper (phenomenology-jwst-early-structure gap); any high-z prediction must be consistent with this CMB-epoch anchor.

The ISW null-test result implicitly constrains the late-time potential decay rate, which feeds back into the kSZ velocity prediction (phenomenology-kSZ-velocity gap) — when that paper is written, the ISW-consistent decay rate narrows the kSZ prediction envelope.

Passing lensing consistency at Planck precision means the entropy-constrained matter power spectrum is not grossly wrong at z~0.5–2; this provides an indirect cross-check supporting the f·σ₈ sealed prediction's plausibility range.
The null-test framework defines exactly what residual patterns EFCLASS must reproduce, converting theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver from an abstract gap to a concrete specification problem.
With 6 new tests all passing, the test scoreboard moves to ~118 active / ~110 survived, maintaining EFC's >93% pass rate; the 8 previously falsified tests remain unchanged.
